purpose: Arm identity is instrument configuration: lane, model, tool access. Sealed rows are never edited - historical identity lives here, not in the rows. Scoring may bucket a tag by era; no pooled score is ever published; a Brier belongs to one forecaster.
grammar: New tags: lane/model/access, access in {searched, cold, advised, unattested, n-a}. unknown is a classification of history, never a forward tag. unattested is a forward tag and means the session COULD have retrieved and the sealed text cites nothing - availability likely, use unevidenced. Prefer searched or cold whenever the run makes access provable. `cadence` records how often an arm is polled; arms with different cadences carry different row counts for that reason and no other.

arms.note: The arm is not trying to be right. It emits the same probability for every row drawn from the same reference class, computed from this ledger's own resolved history as of the pairing date and pre-registered before the outcome existed. Its Brier is the floor a forecaster arm must clear to have demonstrated anything; a forecaster arm that does not beat it has skill zero regardless of its raw score. Paired same-run against the arm it controls, on the identical packet - a control issued later mirrors rows sealed under a different gate and is not a control. Every row carries control_basis: rate, n, reference class, as-of date.
arms.cadence: paired same-run with every sealed forecaster batch; never issued alone, never backfilled.

arms.note: market-implied control arm (KK17 frontier bank, landed KK36): probability read from a named liquid market at seal; rationale must carry market source, level, and read timestamp; rows seal through the same gate; no pooled score.
